tests: Two disposable NATS Server 2.11.4 processes with separate EAST/WEST JetStream domains and a WEST-to-EAST loopback leaf connection.
Executed all published Python fragments inside an async wrapper with nats-py 2.10.0, including shared StreamSource object, domain selection, stream creation, publications and inspection.

Mirror retained source sequence/payload/subject/timestamp for three records; aggregate contained those plus WEST record. Timestamps compared through raw message-get API because pinned Python RawStreamMsg lacks time.
Stopped destination WEST only, published fourth record to EAST, restarted WEST with same store; mirror caught up to four and aggregate to five, source errors absent and lag zero.
Both owned server processes stopped and temporary stores removed.
Eight-edge Mermaid structure checked; 1280x720 generated social image visually reviewed without clipping.
limitations: No real regions, WAN latency, network partition, gateways, TLS, restricted accounts, multi-replica cluster or production promotion tested.
Server snippets used equivalent temporary absolute store paths in harness, not the published relative directory names.
No retention expiry, deletion propagation, cross-domain cycle or consumer-state migration test.
Mermaid checked structurally without graphical rendering.
